finding: In this frozen example, bare I is not explicitly named as the natural-number diagonal before its use in the weak-order unions. Id(A) expands to roman Id with subscript A, not bare I. This is a locally implicit notation transition, not a claim of a false theorem or scan-transcription error.
proof: Let D be the diagonal. L union I = L union D implies D subset I subset L union D. G union I = G union D also implies I subset G union D. Intersecting gives I=D because L and G are disjoint off the diagonal. Either union alone does not uniquely determine I.
